rationale: The three edge surfaces that interact, in one file, because none of them can be pinned properly alone. (1) EXPORTS: `#' @export` above a function and above an ALL-CAPS constant are two different declarations and both are pinned; `private_fn` has no tag and is forbidden, because an exports edge for it would put a name in the package's public surface that no `@export` and no NAMESPACE entry supports. (2) EXTENDS: only `Child2` inherits, so exactly one extends edge exists. `Other2` declares the same member as `Base2` and INHERITS NOTHING -- a rule that treats a shared member name as an override, or that treats a same-file class as a base, produces `overrides Other2 -> render` and `extends Other2 -> Base2`, and both are forbidden here. That second one is the specific fabrication this file exists to catch: co-existence in a file is not inheritance. (3) OVERRIDES: three classes declare a method called `render`, so the TARGET `render` resolves to three published symbols and cannot distinguish them on its own -- which is why the pin carries `overridingMember` and `overriddenMember` in metadata, and why the edge's SOURCE is the derived class. F18 pins the same fact with a three-level chain; here it is pinned alongside the case where no chain exists, so a direction fix that simply always emits an edge would be caught.
